basic.title: Staff Machine Learning Engineer
basic.summary: Hands-on AI/ML leader with 10+ years building production-grade systems that drive measurable business impact. I turn complex ML challenges into scalable, real-world solutions—leading teams to deliver multimodal agents, real-time inference systems, and computer vision pipelines serving millions of users. Deep experience across the full stack: data engineering, model development, MLOps, and applied data science.

experience.title: Staff Machine Learning Engineer, Ads Ranking ML
bullets: Ads Ranking ML is the core monetization engine powering Facebook, Instagram, Messenger, and Audience Network. Most recently, tech lead for the end-to-end ML stack of a conversational advertiser copilot — defining agent contracts, the teacher → student distillation playbook, and shared eval standards adopted across sub-teams. Built on Meta's internal data, training, serving, and observability infrastructure throughout.
- Earlier ads ranking work (2013 – 2022)

Contributed to the evolution of ad CTR / conversion prediction from classical models (logistic regression with feature crosses, GBDTs) toward large-scale deep ranking — including sparse-feature embedding tables and hashing strategies for high-cardinality ad / advertiser / audience signals.

Drove experimentation rigor on ranker A/B tests — guarding against metric peeking, novelty effects, and network interference — and partnered with science on counterfactual offline evaluators that accelerated ranker iteration cycles.
Worked on auction-side modeling (bid-landscape estimation, calibration, value-aware optimization) and on cold-start strategies for new advertisers and creatives.
- Conversational advertiser copilot — architecture & multi-agent orchestration

Made the 0→1 architectural call to break the original single-prompt design into a 7-agent orchestration graph (router, retrieval, planner, creative-gen, ranker, policy, memory) with typed I/O contracts between every node — unlocking per-component evals, controllability, and clean policy isolation.
Defined service-to-service plumbing patterns over gRPC with retry / timeout / circuit-breaker middleware; full per-step execution traces via OpenTelemetry.
Designed the session-state layer over Meta's internal hot-cache + durable-store primitives, using typed normalized campaign schemas so prior valid state persists across refinement turns.
- Modeling

Productionized a two-stage modeling pattern — frontier LLM teachers used for offline research and benchmarking, distilled into fine-tuned open-weight SLMs (Llama-family) for serving — cutting p95 latency 3× and inference cost 5× versus the initial production baseline.

Led training of a multi-turn tool-call extraction model (fine-tuned Llama) that emits normalized API calls — update_budget, set_geo, update_tone — conditioned on prior turns and intermediate tool outputs; PEFT / LoRA / TRL on PyTorch, served via Meta's internal low-latency LLM runtime.

Drove fine-tuning of Llama-family SLMs for ad-copy generation (headlines, primary text, CTAs, tone-constrained rewrites, policy-safe paraphrases) on FSDP, benchmarked against frontier LLM teachers in offline eval.

Stood up an RLHF pipeline (SFT → DPO via TRL + custom PyTorch reward models) over preference signals from advertiser acceptance, human quality ratings, policy compliance, brand-tone fit, and pairwise rewrite annotations — lifting suggestion acceptance materially over SFT-only baselines.
- Data, retrieval, ranking, policy

Defined the synthetic multi-turn data-generation approach — paraphrases, slot overwrites, contradictory follow-ups, edge-case tool sequences — distilled from anonymized workflow traces using large-model teachers; led design of the QC pipeline (JSON-schema validation, diversity filters, slot-replay tests, policy sanity checks, dedup, human spot review) and an experiment registry linking dataset version → model version.
Architected a hybrid retrieval stack — lexical (BM25-style) + dense semantic (FAISS) + a learned reranker — over policy docs, ad templates, product metadata, and historical creative.
Drove design of a campaign knowledge graph (advertiser → campaign → audience → geo → creative → policy) used for grounding and policy lookups, backed by Meta's internal graph and relational stores.

Led the team that shipped creative / template / audience rankers — gradient-boosted baseline migrating to a deep PyTorch ranker over batch-derived features (semantic relevance, vertical match, historical acceptance, policy risk, recency, session preferences) — improving NDCG, MRR, precision@k, and acceptance-weighted rank quality over retrieval-only baselines.

Architected a 3-tier policy validator (rules engine → gradient-boosted classifier → LLM-judge fallback) wired in as a first-class orchestration agent and grounded by RAG over the policy KB + structured policy graph, blocking unsafe content before it surfaces.
- Data platform & feature store

Drove design of the streaming interaction-log pipeline (chat turns, tool calls, accept / reject events, policy outcomes) on Meta's internal stream-processing platform at millions of events / day; batch ETL on the internal Spark-based compute and scheduler, landing partitioned columnar tables on Meta's internal data lake; analyst and ML access via the internal warehouse and federated SQL.

Defined data-quality contracts (schema and value-level expectations + transform tests) with lineage tracked through Meta's internal lineage tooling, plus PII scrubbing / hashing pipelines and access governance via internal data-access controls.

Led design of the online + offline feature store on Meta's internal feature-store primitives, hitting sub-10 ms p99 reads at request time; guaranteed training / serving parity via shared feature definitions, point-in-time joins, and per-feature TTL / freshness SLAs; definitions versioned in source control with CI validation, drift and null-rate regressions tracked on internal observability dashboards.
- Serving, eval, observability

Drove inference-stack optimization — request batching, KV-cache reuse, quantization, and GPU autoscaling on Meta's internal serving platform — to hit sub-second p95 latency at the 5× cost reduction noted above.

Defined the eval harness covering tool-call exact match, slot-level accuracy, overwrite / carry-forward correctness, retrieval recall@k, grounding faithfulness, NDCG / MRR, policy violation rate, and per-stage latency; versioned golden sets and regression suites tracked through Meta's internal experiment-tracking platform.

Led design of online-experiment plumbing — feature-flag allocator + canary + holdout cohorts + counterfactual analysis — across history length, teacher prompts, tool-call schemas, SLM families, rerankers, KG on / off, multi-agent vs single-agent, policy ordering, and clarification thresholds; measured setup time, completion rate, acceptance rate, manual corrections, policy-safe success, satisfaction, session dropoff, and cost per successful session.

Established observability across the agent graph — p50 / p95 / p99 latency, token latency, retrieval misses, hallucination spikes, tool-call schema failures, policy block rate, acceptance regressions, GPU utilization, and cache hit rate — via OpenTelemetry tracing into Meta's internal metrics and dashboarding stack, with runbooks, alerts, and on-call dashboards.
- Platform engineering

Drove CI design — code, tests, lint, image build, plus long-running training and eval jobs — running unit, integration, and eval-regression suites on every change; artifacts shipped through Meta's internal container and deploy infrastructure, with canary + shadow deploys and automated rollback on p95 latency, error rate, policy violation rate, or acceptance regression breaches.
Versioned prompts, tool schemas, and agent configs in source control, gated behind eval-CI golden-set regression thresholds before any production rollout.

Defined dev / staging / prod separation and IaC-style infra definitions on Meta's internal infra primitives, with drift detection in CI; LLM inference on A100 / H100 GPU pools, training on spot + reserved-capacity fallback; per-team cost attribution via internal cost-tracking tooling.
Partnered cross-functionally with product, infra, and research; mentored engineers and led technical reviews advancing generative and multimodal AI across the org.
